verdict: REJECT. The seven-item minimum stands. Build against section 1 as written. Three independent findings carry it, and any one of them would be enough. (1) THE ACCEPTED PLAN ALREADY SETTLES THE SEQUENCING QUESTION, AND SETTLES IT AGAINST THIS SPLIT. Section 2.1's workflow drafts 'GitHub/HF/Kaggle release candidates' at ONE node, audits them once, and publishes once; section 5.1 step 6 stages Hub repositories privately and prepares Kaggle assets privately BEFORE the public step; section 11's R2 requires a Kaggle dataset/notebook candidate and private HF candidates before R3; and section 17's evidence-acceptance checklist requires 'GitHub, Hugging Face and Kaggle drafts are cross-linked and inspected' BEFORE public release. Stage A fails that last box by construction, because under Stage A no HF or Kaggle draft exists to cross-link. The plan does contain the GitHub-first ordering the implementer wants - R3 publishes GitHub, then HF, then the Collection, then Kaggle - so the sequencing is already granted. What is not granted, and what this amendment actually asks for, is deferring the BUILDING of items 5 and 6 behind a second gate. (2) THE BRIGHT LINE IS NOT MERELY POST-HOC, IT IS CONTRADICTED BY THE PLAN. 'Items 5 and 6 are distribution, not contribution' is refuted in as many words by section 7.1: 'Kaggle will not be a redundant model mirror by default. Its distinctive contribution is an accessible, CPU-compatible learning artifact.' Section 7.2 then imposes eleven requirements on that notebook, several of which - plain-language explanation of alpha, delta, selected risk, acceptance and Infeasible; the conservative audit shown beside the preferred certifier; an educational walkthrough - are content that exists nowhere in items 1-4. Item 6 is not a copy of item 2 or item 3. The implementer flagged this objection as the strongest against its own proposal and could not answer it; it cannot be answered, because the accepted plan pre-emptively rejects its premise. (3) THE AMENDMENT PROPOSES THE ONE ROUTE THE PLAN DOES NOT AUTHORISE WHILE NOT CITING THE TWO IT DOES. Section 15 is a table of reduced-but-honest releases, and it already contemplates dropping item 6 - 'Kaggle environment cannot run method -> smaller validated CPU fixture or omit notebook until it can pass'. Section 17's first evidence-acceptance line reads 'Plans 1-3 implementation/evidence gates pass OR THE RELEASE SCOPE IS REDUCED EXPLICITLY'. So the seven are reducible; the plan says how. Both routes are failure-triggered and owner-declared, and neither is triggered by the road being long. Reinterpreting the word 'minimum' is the one mechanism the plan does not provide, and it is the one the amendment chose. Two further matters are recorded rather than blocking: the accepted plan states 'the minimum contribution' TWICE with different contents (section 1 lists seven; section 17's ticked direction-acceptance box names three - evaluator/certifier, evidence bundle, CPU replay), which is a real defect in the authority and needs its own dated amendment, not a licence for either party to pick a reading; and the amendment's staleness argument miscites this repository's own record (finding 6). The amendment is honestly written, states the case against itself accurately, and cost nothing to reject, which is exactly what was asked of it. Rejecting it is not a criticism of routing it.

question_1_does_section_1_permit_a_stage.the_primary_text: Section 1 reads 'The minimum useful public contribution is:' followed by the seven numbered items. The governed noun is 'public contribution' - one object - and 'minimum' qualifies its composition, not its schedule. Read in isolation the sentence is genuinely ambiguous between 'the floor for the first public act' and 'the floor for the release as a whole'. It contains no word of sequence: not 'in stages', not 'at least', and equally not 'simultaneously' or 'before any is published'. The implementer is right that section 1 alone does not decide this, and right to have said so rather than asserting the reading it preferred.
question_1_does_section_1_permit_a_stage.what_section_1_does_settle: One thing. The paragraph immediately after the list handles the QLoRA adapter as a conditional extra - 'It strengthens the release but is not allowed to become a single point of failure' - and the paragraph after that makes a hosted Space explicitly optional. Section 1 therefore knows how to mark an item as conditional or optional, and marks none of the seven that way. That is weak evidence for the whole-release reading, not decisive on its own.
question_1_does_section_1_permit_a_stage.section_2_1_cuts_against_the_split: DECIDES PART OF IT. The release workflow is a single linear pipeline: 'draft GitHub/HF/Kaggle release candidates -> licence, privacy and link audit -> public versioned release -> anonymous fresh-download verification'. All three surfaces are drafted at ONE node, and ONE licence/privacy/link audit stands between that node and publication. Under Stage A/B the pipeline runs twice, and the audit protecting items 5 and 6 would post-date the publication of items 1-4. That is not a fatal objection by itself - running a pipeline twice is not forbidden - but it is the plan's own picture of the release, and the picture has one public act in it.
question_1_does_section_1_permit_a_stage.section_2_2_does_not_settle_it: SILENT, and honestly so. The mandatory level is Result replay: 'a CPU user can regenerate certificates, tables and figures from immutable released predictions/results'. Items 2 and 3 satisfy that inside the repository. Nothing in 2.2 requires Kaggle or the Hub. This is the strongest thing in sections 2.1-2.3 for the implementer's side and it should be said plainly: on reproducibility grounds alone, Stage A would be a sufficient release.
question_1_does_section_1_permit_a_stage.section_2_3_does_not_settle_it: SILENT. 2.3 governs which OUTCOMES can support a release - and confirms that this project's outcome, 'all systems are infeasible', is release-worthy. It says nothing about the composition or timing of artifacts.
what_actually_settles_it: SECTION 5.1 STEP 6: 'stage Hub repositories privately and prepare Kaggle assets privately/draft where supported' - a numbered step in the release sequence, before step 8's publish.

SECTION 11, STAGE R2: 'Upload private Hugging Face evidence/model candidates. Prepare Kaggle dataset/notebook candidate. Populate provisional cross-links and perform licence/claim review.' R2 precedes R3. Under Stage A the repository is published at R3 with R2 half-executed.

SECTION 17, EVIDENCE ACCEPTANCE BEFORE PUBLIC RELEASE: '[ ] GitHub, Hugging Face and Kaggle drafts are cross-linked and inspected.' This is the decisive line. It is an unticked box in the accepted plan, its heading is 'before public release', and Stage A cannot tick it, because Stage A defers the existence of the HF and Kaggle drafts to Stage B. The amendment does not mention this box.

SECTION 11, STAGE R3: publish GitHub, then the HF evidence Dataset, then the Collection, then Kaggle, then 'update all cross-links and manifest URLs'. So the plan already grants GitHub-first ordering. The thing the implementer wants at publication time is already in the plan and needed no amendment.
question_1_does_section_1_permit_a_stage.ruling: 'Minimum useful public contribution' is a floor for the release as a whole, not for the first public act. Section 1 alone does not carry that; sections 5.1, 11 and 17 do, and they carry it specifically against the proposed split because Stage A cannot satisfy section 17's cross-linked-drafts box by construction. The plan permits GitHub to go public FIRST. It does not permit items 5 and 6 to be UNBUILT when that happens.

the_internal_inconsistency_i_am_obliged_.what: The accepted plan says 'the minimum contribution' twice, with different contents. Section 1 lists seven items. Section 17's direction-acceptance checklist - the ticked boxes, i.e. the acceptance instrument itself, accepted 2026-07-15 per the acceptance addendum - contains '[x] The evaluator/certifier, evidence bundle and CPU replay are the minimum contribution.' That names items 1, 2 and 3 only. It omits the GitHub release, both mirrors and the report.
the_internal_inconsistency_i_am_obliged_.why_i_am_raising_it_when_neither_party_d: It is the single strongest piece of text in the repository for the proposition that section 1's list is not an indivisible unit, and the implementer did not find it. A reviewer who rejects a proposal without disclosing the best argument for it is not ruling adversarially, only unfavourably.
why_it_does_not_rescue_the_amendment: It names a DIFFERENT set. Section 17's three are items 1-3; Stage A is items 1-4 plus a draft of 7. Neither party's line is the checklist's line, so the checklist endorses no proposed split - it would license dropping item 4, which the amendment keeps.

It is a checklist compression of a section, and CLAUDE.md records by name what this repository lost the last time a ruling was taken from a gloss rather than the section: 'the repo's gloss on 6.3 was stricter than 6.3 actually is, and an ADR was written against the gloss.' Section 1 is the section. Section 17 is the gloss. The direction of the error is reversed here - this gloss is laxer, not stricter - which makes it more tempting to rely on, not less.
An inconsistency in the authority is a reason to fix the authority. It is not a licence for either the implementer or this seat to adopt whichever of the two readings suits it.
the_internal_inconsistency_i_am_obliged_.what_should_happen_to_it: Recorded as required item R3. It wants a dated amendment note against section 17, in the same appended-not-rewritten form as the 2026-07-29 status amendment, reconciling the two statements of 'the minimum contribution'. That is its own change and needs its own review. It must NOT be folded into a release commit, and this record does not resolve it.

question_2_why_5_and_6_and_not_4.the_line_under_test: The amendment's reply to its own strongest objection: '5 and 6 are the only two items whose ENTIRE CONTENT is a copy of another item, which is a bright line, but it is a line drawn after the fact.'
question_2_why_5_and_6_and_not_4.ruling: THE LINE IS NOT PRINCIPLED, AND THE MORE SERIOUS PROBLEM IS THAT IT IS NOT ACCURATE. It fails on the facts before it fails on principle, and it fails against the accepted plan's own text rather than against my judgement.
item_6_is_not_a_copy_of_anything: SECTION 7.1 REJECTS THE PREMISE BY NAME: 'Kaggle will not be a redundant model mirror by default. Its distinctive contribution is an accessible, CPU-compatible learning artifact' - and then: 'This makes the work useful to practitioners who cannot reproduce QLoRA training.' The plan considered the mirror characterisation and refused it in the section that governs item 6.

SECTION 7.2 IMPOSES ELEVEN REQUIREMENTS ON THE NOTEBOOK, and at least four describe content that exists in no other item: 'explain alpha, delta, selected risk, acceptance and Infeasible in plain language'; 'show the conservative audit next to the preferred certifier'; 'label the shift result as an uncertified stress test'; 'state what cannot be reconstructed because of licence restrictions'. Item 3's notebook (section 3.2: notebooks/reproduce_release.ipynb) is specified in section 1 as reproducing 'the certificate, result tables and figures from released evidence without retraining' - a replay artifact, not an explanatory one. Item 6's notebook must also 'reconstruct the headline certificate/table/figure, not merely display saved images', which means it is not a copy of item 3's OUTPUT either.
CONSEQUENCE: item 6 is the largest genuinely new writing in items 5-7 and the one item in the deferred set that carries content found nowhere else. Deferring it is the opposite of deferring a copy.
item_5_is_the_closer_case_and_still_fail: The dataset half is close to a copy. Section 6.1's expected contents overlap item 2's bundle heavily - manifest, claim ledger, aggregate tables, configs, fixtures, notebook inputs. If the argument had been made about the HF DATASET alone it would have had real force, and I would have had to weigh it.

But item 5 as written in section 1 is 'a Hugging Face evidence Dataset repository AND COLLECTION'. Section 6.3: 'Create one Hugging Face Collection linking the evidence dataset, adapter if public, GitHub release, and any later Space or paper.' A Collection is not a copy of anything - it is the index, and the index cannot exist until there is more than one surface to index.

The plan's stated PURPOSE, first line of the document, names this as a goal in its own right: 'connect GitHub/Hugging Face/Kaggle into one evidence trail'. Section 13's exit artifact for the Public-contribution track is a 'connected public contribution set'. Section 3.2: Git holds compact evidence, the Hub and Kaggle hold approved larger replay assets, 'all connected by hashes and immutable revisions'. Connectedness is a named deliverable, and Stage A delivers one node of it.
question_2_why_5_and_6_and_not_4.the_principled_line_the_plan_does_draw_a: Section 3.1 does distinguish canonical from non-canonical: GitHub carries 'source, tests, methods, report and canonical version history'. That is a real line and item 4 sits on the canonical side of it. But the plan draws it to decide WHERE ARTIFACTS LIVE and how storage duplication is minimised (section 14: 'large artifacts are kept in one canonical home with links elsewhere'), not to rank items by necessity. Being non-canonical is not being redundant; section 7.1 says so directly.
question_2_why_5_and_6_and_not_4.on_the_general_objection: The implementer's self-stated worry - 'the staging argument is available for any item... a plan that yields to that argument once has no principled stopping point' - is correct, and I am adopting it rather than softening it. Once 'this could ship later' is a sufficient reason, item 4 is next (a tag is a copy of the tree), then item 3 (a notebook is a copy of the library's outputs), and the floor is items 1 and 2. Nothing in the amendment's reasoning stops that regression, and the fallback bright line does not exist.
question_2_why_5_and_6_and_not_4.what_i_am_NOT_saying: I am not ruling that items 5 and 6 must be built. I am ruling that the copy-of-another-item argument cannot be the reason they are not. The plan's own reduction routes remain open and are set out in finding 7.

question_3_is_the_dependency_correctly_s.the_stated_dependency: 'Stage A includes item 2, and what item 2 CONTAINS is exactly decision 1, so Stage A cannot be executed until decision 1 is answered by Ross.'
question_3_is_the_dependency_correctly_s.is_it_true: YES, and it is stated well. Decision 1 in open-release-decisions.md is 'Do reviewer records ship in the public evidence bundle?' Item 2 is 'an immutable, licence-safe evidence bundle with manifests, aggregate results and claim status'. The mapping is exact, the direction of the dependency is right, and declaring it in the 'what this amendment does not do' section - rather than leaving a reader to derive it - is the correct instinct and the best-executed paragraph in the document.
question_3_is_the_dependency_correctly_s.is_it_complete: NO. Three further dependencies are undeclared, and one of them is larger than the one that is declared.

undeclared_dependency_1_plan_4_has_not_o.what: The gated doctrine in CLAUDE.md: 'Plan N+1 starts only after Plan N's independent reviewer PASS'. The accepted plan's own 2026-07-29 amendment records Plan 3 as 'executed and independently reviewed, NOT FORMALLY CLOSED - five Plan 3 reviewer records exist and none carries review_kind: plan_close'. open-release-decisions.md closes with 'Both items are gated behind Plan 4 opening, and Plan 4 has not opened.' The write-up draft's status block says 'starting Plan 4 remains unauthorised', and the writeup-draft reviewer record's discharge explicitly does not authorise 'Starting Plan 4, advancing any gate, or closing Plan 3.'
undeclared_dependency_1_plan_4_has_not_o.why_it_matters_here: Stage A is release execution. It cannot begin until Plan 3 is formally closed and Plan 4 opens. The amendment restructures the composition of a plan that has not opened, in order to accelerate work that cannot start, and does not say so. That is not a fatal defect in a proposal - planning ahead of a gate is legitimate - but 'Stage A cannot be executed until decision 1 is answered' names a smaller blocker while a larger one goes unmentioned, and a reader could reasonably infer decision 1 is the last thing standing in the way. It is not.

undeclared_dependency_2_decision_2_is_fo.what: Stage A makes the repository public. open-release-decisions.md decision 2 concerns the repository description, is open, and the description is currently empty; decision 3 concerns topics, is open, and there are none. The decision document's own framing is that these 'must be made BEFORE anything is published' and that a description is 'rendered on every search result, every listing, and every link preview'.
undeclared_dependency_2_decision_2_is_fo.why_it_matters: The amendment is correct that it does not SETTLE decision 2 in words. But executing Stage A settles it in fact, by shipping the default - an empty description - as the answer. Choosing a default by acting is still choosing. Decision 3 has the same shape and lower stakes: 'no topics' is a defensible non-claim in a way that a wrong description is not.
undeclared_dependency_2_decision_2_is_fo.severity: Real, and not bad faith. It is a consequence of the staging, not a concealment in it. Under any staged scheme this must be declared alongside decision 1.

undeclared_dependency_3_the_section_17_c.what: Section 17's evidence-acceptance list is twelve unticked boxes gating public release: V1-V11 against one frozen candidate, immutable manifest and checksums, licence/provenance matrix, CPU result replay, identical approved claims across GitHub/cards/notebook/report, 'GitHub, Hugging Face and Kaggle drafts are cross-linked and inspected', and recorded public V12 verification.
undeclared_dependency_3_the_section_17_c.why_it_matters: The amendment discusses which ITEMS ship in which stage and never touches which GATES each stage must pass. At minimum a staged scheme must say what Stage A does with the cross-linked-drafts box, which it cannot tick, and with V12, which is a post-publication check that would have to run twice. As written, the amendment leaves an implementer to infer that Stage A inherits the whole checklist, including a box it cannot satisfy.

question_3_is_the_dependency_correctly_s.one_internal_inconsistency_in_the_docume: Under 'Proposal': 'Stage A would make the repository public.' Under 'What this amendment does not do': 'It does not flip repository visibility. That is Ross's action, not this plan's.' Both sentences are defensible - the plan authorises, the owner acts - but together they blur the one thing the document is actually for. The 'The question' section opens with 'Ross wants the repository public', which is the motivation for the whole proposal; a document motivated by visibility should not also disclaim visibility. See finding 7 for why this matters more than a drafting nit.

question_4_does_it_smuggle_a_decision.decision_1_reviewer_records: NOT SMUGGLED. Declared explicitly, in its own bullet, with the dependency stated in the direction that constrains the implementer rather than the direction that frees it. This is the amendment's best paragraph and it should be preserved in whatever record survives this rejection.
question_4_does_it_smuggle_a_decision.decision_2_description: NOT SETTLED IN WORDS; FORCED IN PRACTICE. See question 3. Executing Stage A publishes an empty description, which is the default answer to an open decision. The amendment should have declared this and did not.
question_4_does_it_smuggle_a_decision.decision_3_topics: SAME SHAPE, LOWER STAKES. Publishing with no topics ships the default. 'No topics' asserts nothing, so the honesty exposure is materially smaller than decision 2's - but it is still an open decision answered by acting.

two_claim_shaped_assertions_that_are_not.framing: Neither is a public claim and neither blocks anything. Both are recorded because they are the defect class this repository keeps finding in its own prose - assertion-shaped sentences with no artifact behind them - and because the same class was raised against the write-up draft eight days earlier and required scoping there.
two_claim_shaped_assertions_that_are_not.a: 'If item 2 is sound, a reader can verify every claim from the GitHub release alone.' Item 2 does not exist. Its soundness is a hypothetical, and the sentence is doing load-bearing work in the argument for deferring the mirrors. The conditional is honest as far as it goes, but the conclusion is stated with more confidence than a conditional on a non-existent artifact supports.
two_claim_shaped_assertions_that_are_not.b: 'Staging surfaces defects earlier. A public repository gets read.' This repository has no audience and no evidence about one. That is a prediction, not an argument from the record, and it sits in the case-FOR section without a hedge while the case-AGAINST section hedges scrupulously. Compare the writeup-draft record's required item W6, which forced exactly this kind of forward-looking comparative out of the draft's opening.

question_5_stage_a_item_7.status: MOOT ON THE RULING - staging is rejected, so item 7 is one of seven items to be built in full. Ruled anyway, because the question was put and because the answer holds under any future staging proposal.
question_5_stage_a_item_7.ruling_if_staging_had_been_accepted: THE EXISTING DRAFT COULD NOT HAVE STOOD IN FOR ITEM 7, and the reason is not the draft's quality - it is that the draft is not the same object.
reasoning: ITEM 7 IS TWO ARTIFACTS, NOT ONE: 'a paper-shaped technical report AND outcome-conditional portfolio narrative'. The portfolio narrative is specified in sections 12.2 and 12.3 - one evidence-matched CV bullet chosen after results, plus 60-second, 3-minute and 10-minute interview walkthroughs. None of it exists. Section 12.2's infeasible/null bullet is the applicable one and it is a template. So the draft is a partial version of one of item 7's two halves.

THE REPORT HALF IS NOT PAPER-SHAPED YET IN THE PLAN'S SENSE. Section 8.1 fixes a ten-part structure (problem and falsifiable question; relationship to prior work; same-backbone systems and leakage controls; evaluator, loss and score; certificate and assumptions; preregistered in-domain comparisons; frozen transfer under shift; results and failure taxonomy; compute/cost and reproducibility; limitations, ethics, licences and future work). The draft is six sections plus a generated appendix and does not attempt that structure.

THE DRAFT SAYS SO ITSELF: 'Status: FIRST DRAFT, 2026-07-28, revision 2. Not a submission. No venue is chosen and nothing here is formatted for one. This is not a Plan 4 artifact.' Its reviewer record's discharge authorises committing it and nothing else, and lists 'Publication, submission or posting anywhere' under does_not_authorise.

WHAT THE DRAFT IS: a genuinely good and independently reviewed BLOCK-to-discharge write-up whose claim discipline survived a hostile forbidden-table re-walk with zero hits. Its absence of a venue is not the defect - section 8.3's publication ladder puts a versioned GitHub technical report FIRST and arXiv fourth and optional, so a venueless report is exactly what the plan asks for. The defect is scope: it is one half of item 7, unfinished, not item 7.
question_5_stage_a_item_7.the_narrow_thing_that_would_have_been_de: Had staging been accepted, 'a draft of 7' could honestly have meant: the report half at draft status, PLUS the section 12.2 CV bullet chosen and evidence-matched, PLUS an explicit public statement in the repository that the report is a draft and the portfolio narrative is incomplete. What could not be defended is calling the existing file 'item 7 (draft)' when half of item 7 has not been started. Recording this so that a future staging proposal does not re-open the question in a weaker form.

question_6_is_the_goes_stale_argument_ho.the_sentence: 'They are the items most likely to go stale. This repository has now produced FOUR DOCUMENTED INSTANCES of a record drifting from what it describes. A mirror on a third-party host is a fifth opportunity, on infrastructure with no test suite and no reviewer.'
question_6_is_the_goes_stale_argument_ho.ruling: THE UNDERLYING WORRY IS REAL. THE SENTENCE THAT CARRIES IT IS NOT SUPPORTED BY THE RECORD IT CITES, AND IT FAILS THE GATE IT IS BORROWING FROM. This is the one place where the amendment does the thing this repository exists to catch, and it does it while citing the check designed to catch it.

what_the_record_actually_holds.the_four: REVIEW.md's scope-matches-sentence gate: 'Four instances on 2026-07-28 - a cost total that omitted a figure recoverable from citations the same change had just added; a draft asserting a citation count that a later fix made stale; a hygiene report that introduced the paths it existed to remove, unseen by its own git grep; and the reviewer record diagnosing all three, which asserted a repository-wide zero on the strength of a scan it had not run.' NONE of these four is a copy drifting from an original. All four are a CHECK'S SCOPE failing to cover its own SENTENCE, inside one repository, with no mirror or duplicate involved.
what_the_record_actually_holds.the_three: A different REVIEW.md gate holds the drift instances: 'A document that asserts a gate state must be reconciled before it is used. THREE INSTANCES NOW: the README said Plan 1 is active through Plan 3; main sat eleven days behind the branch that corrected it; and docs/plan4/accepted-plan.md opened Plan 4 still saying Plans 1-3 were not implemented.'
what_the_record_actually_holds.the_defect: The amendment takes the COUNT from the scope-matches-sentence gate and the DESCRIPTION from the gate-state gate. Four instances exist; they are not instances of drift. Three drift instances exist; they are not four. The sentence's scope does not match its evidence, which is the precise failure mode REVIEW.md places above everything else and describes as firing 'at the START of a review'.

question_6_is_the_goes_stale_argument_ho.the_honest_core_that_survives: ONE cited instance is a genuine and close analogue, and it is the strongest thing available to the argument: 'main sat eleven days behind the branch that corrected it, so THE ONLY STORY A READER COULD REACH WAS THE WRONG ONE.' That is exactly the mirror failure mode - a stale public copy while the corrected version sits somewhere the reader cannot see. Argued from that one instance, and named as one, the staleness worry would have been well founded and I would have credited it. Inflated to four and re-described as drift, it converts a real argument into an unchecked one.
question_6_is_the_goes_stale_argument_ho.the_argument_the_amendment_does_not_enga: The plan has already answered staleness, by design, in the paragraph the amendment would have had to overcome. Section 3.2: the Hub and Kaggle hold approved replay assets 'all connected by HASHES and IMMUTABLE REVISIONS'. Section 5.1 step 10: 'record any correction as a new version; NEVER SILENTLY REPLACE IMMUTABLE EVIDENCE.' Section 9.3 specifies the correction and withdrawal procedure across surfaces, including marking affected claim IDs as disputed and updating cards and cross-links. Section 6.4 requires a download-and-replay test from a clean cache. Immutable pinned revisions are the standard answer to mirror drift, they are in the plan, and the amendment neither cites nor rebuts them.
question_6_is_the_goes_stale_argument_ho.and_it_cuts_the_other_way: The amendment's own case-against concedes 'Stage B may never happen' and that the evidence trail becomes 'GitHub plus two promises'. An indefinitely deferred mirror is a worse instance of the same failure than a mirror pinned by hash at a known revision: the promise has no checksum. The staleness argument, taken seriously, is an argument for building 5 and 6 with pinned revisions and against deferring them.
question_6_is_the_goes_stale_argument_ho.verdict: PARTLY HONEST, PARTLY RECRUITED. A real anxiety with one genuinely fitting precedent, stated with a count it does not have, in a class it does not belong to, against a mechanism the plan already contains. Required item R2 covers what must happen to the sentence if the document is kept.

question_7_what_the_repository_loses_if_.framing: Stated plainly so the owner can weigh this ruling rather than receive it. I have tried to make this section as strong as the implementer would have made it.

what_building_all_seven_costs.item_5_hugging_face: Moderate and mostly mechanical, and the smallest of the three. Section 6.1's dataset contents are largely a selection from item 2's bundle, so the writing is the dataset card (provenance, structure, licences, limitations, responsible-use). Section 6.4 then requires an authenticated namespace check, an exact post-upload revision, a file inventory with hashes, `hf cache verify` or equivalent, a download-and-replay from a clean cache, and card-render and link checks. The Collection is minutes. CPU only. No spend.
what_building_all_seven_costs.item_6_kaggle: THE LARGEST GENUINELY NEW PIECE OF WORK IN THE DEFERRED SET, and the amendment's framing hid this from itself. Section 7.2's eleven requirements include a notebook that runs top to bottom in a clean Kaggle CPU session, validates manifest hashes before analysis, RECONSTRUCTS the headline certificate and table and figure rather than displaying saved images, explains alpha/delta/selected risk/acceptance/Infeasible in plain language, shows the conservative audit beside the preferred certifier, labels shift as an uncertified stress test, finishes inside a declared CPU budget, and contains no claim absent from the ledger. That is a real writing and engineering job. It is also the item most likely to hit a genuine wall, which is why section 15 already names the exit.
what_building_all_seven_costs.item_7_finished: The report per section 8.1's ten-part structure, plus the section 12.2 CV bullet and the three section 12.3 interview walkthroughs, none of which exist. The draft is a strong start on one half.
what_building_all_seven_costs.money: ZERO, on the plan's own accounting. Section 14: CPU for tests, replay, cards, report and the Kaggle notebook; no standing GPU; no hosted endpoint. The 25 dollar aggregate cap is untouched by any of this. THE COST OF REJECTION IS CALENDAR TIME, NOT BUDGET. That is worth saying because it removes the one consideration that would have weighed heaviest.

what_the_delay_costs_in_substance: Nothing is public for longer, so nothing is read for longer, and the amendment is right that a public repository gets defects found. Against that: the repository has just absorbed four scope-matches-sentence defects and three gate-state defects found WITHOUT any external reader, by its own gates and reviewers. The marginal defect-finding value of an audience this repository does not yet have is speculative; the internal apparatus is demonstrably working.

Momentum. Deferred work in a portfolio has a poor completion record, and that argument is symmetrical: it is the amendment's own stated reason for doubting Stage B would happen. It applies equally to items 5 and 6 whether they are deferred by an accepted amendment or by a rejected one.

There is a real risk I am imposing: if items 5 and 6 turn out to be more work than they look, the seven-item minimum could keep the repository invisible for a long time. I am not indifferent to that, and it is precisely why finding 7's next paragraph matters.

what_rejection_does_NOT_cost_and_this_is.the_finding: THE SEVEN-ITEM MINIMUM WAS NEVER WHAT WAS KEEPING THE REPOSITORY PRIVATE. Section 1 governs 'the minimum useful public CONTRIBUTION' - the release. Repository visibility is not one of the seven items, is not mentioned in section 1, and appears nowhere in sections 11's stages as a gated object. The amendment half-sees this and says both 'Stage A would make the repository public' and 'It does not flip repository visibility. That is Ross's action, not this plan's.' Both cannot be the operative sentence.
what_rejection_does_NOT_cost_and_this_is.consequence: The proposal answered the question 'may we ship fewer than seven items?' when the motivating problem was 'Ross wants the repository public'. Those are different questions with different gates. Making the repository visible is constrained by V8 licences, V9 secrets/PII, the operator-path gate now enforced by tests/test_internal_paths.py, decisions 2 and 3, and the fact that every prose surface in the repository becomes readable at that moment - NOT by whether a Kaggle notebook exists.
what_rejection_does_NOT_cost_and_this_is.what_i_am_explicitly_NOT_doing: I am not ruling that a bare visibility flip is permitted. I have not reviewed it, nobody asked me to, and it would expose the README, docs/ and the write-up draft as live public surfaces - which is a substantial claims question, not a settings change. docs/release-check-2026-07-28.md records that the README is currently 'a PROSPECTIVE public surface, not a live one', and turning that from prospective to live is exactly the sort of change this repository routes. It needs its own proposal and its own review.
what_rejection_does_NOT_cost_and_this_is.why_it_belongs_in_this_record_anyway: Because the owner is being asked to weigh a rejection whose apparent cost is 'the repository stays private'. That is not what my ruling does. It is the honest answer to question 7 and it is more useful to the owner than the ruling itself.

the_two_doors_the_plan_already_provides.framing: The seven are not immutable. The plan says how to ship fewer, twice, and the amendment cites neither. Both are the owner's to open, on a named trigger, with a review.
the_two_doors_the_plan_already_provides.door_1_section_15: The reduced-but-honest release table. The row that fits item 6 exactly: 'Kaggle environment cannot run method -> smaller validated CPU fixture or OMIT NOTEBOOK UNTIL IT CAN PASS; never publish decorative output only.' Also relevant: 'report not ready for arXiv -> publish versioned technical report only.' The trigger is an attempt that fails, not an attempt not yet made.
the_two_doors_the_plan_already_provides.door_2_section_17: The first evidence-acceptance line: 'Plans 1-3 implementation/evidence gates pass OR THE RELEASE SCOPE IS REDUCED EXPLICITLY.' There is live material here that the amendment never raised: ADR 0010 descoped evaluate-final and evaluate-shift, CX-SHIFT-01 is `planned` with no surfaces, and Plan 3 is not formally closed. Whether that constitutes a Plans 1-3 gate shortfall requiring an EXPLICIT reduction of release scope is a real question, it is the owner's to raise, and it would need its own review. I make no finding on it - I am recording that the door exists and that this proposal walked past it.
the_two_doors_the_plan_already_provides.the_distinction_that_matters: Both doors reduce the seven by DECLARING the reduction and its trigger, in the open, as a scope change. The amendment instead re-read the word 'minimum' so that seven items became five without a declared reduction. The outcome might have looked similar; the record it leaves does not. That difference is the whole of this ruling.

question_8_scope.does_the_amendment_change_any_claim: NO. Zero claim IDs cited, zero FORBIDDEN_WORDINGS matches, no metric, no result, no system named. verify-claims unchanged at 14 claims / 12 publishable, exit 0, ok true, unresolved_evidence {}, untracked_evidence {}.
question_8_scope.does_it_change_any_boundary: NO. docs/plan3/certification-result.md's permitted and forbidden lists are untouched and unreferenced. The honesty boundary, the infeasibility framing and the not-production-grade line are not engaged.
question_8_scope.does_it_change_any_evidence_artifact: NO. `git status --porcelain` -> one untracked file. `git diff --name-only HEAD` -> empty. No file under evidence/, src/, tests/, configs/ or docs/adr/ is modified. tests/test_doc_references.py includes test_the_accepted_plans_are_unmodified for all four plans and passes, so the accepted plans are provably untouched.
question_8_scope.is_it_itself_release_work: NO. It creates no Hugging Face repository, no Kaggle dataset, no tag, no release draft, no manifest and no bundle. It does not flip repository visibility. It proposes and requests a ruling; it acts on nothing.
question_8_scope.does_it_open_plan_4_or_advance_a_gate: NO, and it does not claim to. It correctly leaves Plan 3's non-closure and Plan 4's non-opening where they are - though it also does not DECLARE them as blockers, which is recorded under question 3.
question_8_scope.green_command: uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy -> exit 0. 353 passed in 18.97s; 'All checks passed!'; 'Success: no issues found in 24 source files'. As expected.
question_8_scope.verify_claims: uv run conformalextract verify-claims -> exit 0, 14 claims / 12 publishable. As expected.
question_8_scope.spend: 0 dollars. No job submitted, no artifact regenerated, no model loaded. The 25 dollar aggregate cap is untouched.
question_8_scope.sealed_data: Not read by the amendment and not read by this review. No command touching the `certification`, `final` or `shift` roles was executed. No evidence artifact hash changed.
question_8_scope.verdict: SCOPE IS CLEAN, and this is the amendment's strongest property. A proposal to change a plan that changes nothing until it is ruled on is exactly the right shape, and it was routed before being acted on, which is what the owner asked for and what the doctrine requires.

R1_THE_RULING.what: Build against docs/plan4/accepted-plan.md section 1 as written. The minimum useful public contribution is seven items and they are the composition of the release, not of its first act. Sections 5.1 step 6, 11 (R2 and R3) and 17 fix the ORDER - HF and Kaggle candidates staged and cross-linked privately, GitHub published first at R3, then the HF Dataset, then the Collection, then Kaggle - so the GitHub-first sequencing the amendment wanted is already granted and needs no amendment.
R1_THE_RULING.consequence_for_the_implementer: No staged A/B gate. No second review gate between a GitHub release and the mirrors. Items 5 and 6 are built and staged privately before the public act, per R2.

R2_THE_MISCITED_SENTENCE.what: 'This repository has now produced four documented instances of a record drifting from what it describes' is not supported. REVIEW.md's four 2026-07-28 instances are scope-matches-sentence failures, not drift; the drift instances are the gate-state gate's three, of which exactly one - main sitting eleven days behind the branch that corrected it - is a genuine stale-copy analogue. If this document is committed as part of the record, correct the sentence to cite the one instance that fits and name its gate, or annotate it. If the document is discarded, nothing is required.
R2_THE_MISCITED_SENTENCE.why_it_is_called_out_this_hard: It is a claim whose scope exceeds its evidence, inside an argument, citing the gate that exists to catch exactly that, one commit after 68440df added four tests enforcing that gate. REVIEW.md: 'Before writing a verdict, say which command produced it and what that command cannot see.'

R3_THE_AUTHORITY_IS_INTERNALLY_INCONSIST.file: docs/plan4/accepted-plan.md, section 1 versus section 17 'Direction acceptance now'
R3_THE_AUTHORITY_IS_INTERNALLY_INCONSIST.what: The accepted plan states 'the minimum contribution' twice with different contents: seven items in section 1, three in the ticked box '[x] The evaluator/certifier, evidence bundle and CPU replay are the minimum contribution.' This is a genuine defect in the governing document and neither party found it. It wants a dated amendment note in the appended-not-rewritten form of the 2026-07-29 status amendment, reconciling the two and saying which governs.
R3_THE_AUTHORITY_IS_INTERNALLY_INCONSIST.constraints: It is its own change and needs its own independent review. It must NOT be folded into a release commit and must NOT be treated as reopening this ruling: section 17's three-item set is not Stage A's five-item set, so it endorses no proposed split. Until it is reconciled, section 1 governs, because CLAUDE.md records what this repository lost the last time a ruling was taken from a paraphrase rather than the section.

R4_DO_NOT_READ_THIS_REJECTION_AS_GATING_.what: Repository visibility is not among the seven items and is not gated by them. If the goal is a public repository, that is a different question with different gates (V8, V9, the operator-path gate, open decisions 2 and 3, and the conversion of every prose surface from prospective to live). It needs its own proposal and its own review. This record does not authorise it, and does not forbid it either - it was not put to me.

R5_DECLARE_THE_FULL_DEPENDENCY_SET_NEXT_.what: Any future proposal that sequences release work must declare, alongside decision 1: that Plan 3 is not formally closed and Plan 4 has not opened; that publishing the repository answers open decisions 2 and 3 by default; and what it does with section 17's twelve evidence-acceptance boxes, in particular 'GitHub, Hugging Face and Kaggle drafts are cross-linked and inspected', which no GitHub-only stage can tick.

R6_IF_A_FUTURE_REDUCTION_IS_WANTED_USE_T.what: Section 15's reduced-but-honest table (including 'Kaggle environment cannot run method -> ... omit notebook until it can pass') and section 17's 'Plans 1-3 implementation/evidence gates pass OR the release scope is reduced explicitly'. Both are failure-triggered and owner-declared. A reduction routed that way is a recorded scope change with a named trigger; a reduction obtained by re-reading 'minimum' is not, and is what was rejected here.

does_authorise: Building against the seven-item minimum, in the order the accepted plan already fixes (sections 5.1, 11 R2/R3).

Committing docs/plan4/proposed-amendment-staged-release.md as a rejected proposal alongside this record, if the owner wants the deliberation on the record - subject to R2. The doctrine favours keeping it: a rejected proposal that states the case against itself accurately is a better record than its absence.
Discarding the amendment instead. Either is fine; the ruling is the same.
does_not_authorise: Starting Plan 4, closing Plan 3, advancing any gate, or ticking any section 17 box.
Flipping repository visibility, publishing anything to GitHub, Hugging Face or Kaggle, or creating any external artifact.
Answering open decisions 1, 2 or 3, by act or by implication.
Any edit to docs/plan4/accepted-plan.md, evidence/plan4/claim_ledger.json, src/, tests/, or any evidence artifact. R3 is a recommendation for a separately reviewed change, not a licence to make it.
what_this_review_does_and_does_not_autho.re_review_condition: NONE for this proposal - REJECT is terminal for it and the implementer can build immediately against section 1. R3 needs a new review when someone takes it up. A materially different staging proposal that engages section 17's cross-linked-drafts box, section 7.1's refusal of the mirror characterisation, and the two reduction doors would be a new proposal and would get a fresh reading, not an appeal of this one.

scope: This ruling covers exactly one untracked file at HEAD 128e52c on branch codex/plan4-release: docs/plan4/proposed-amendment-staged-release.md. It rules on whether that proposed amendment to the accepted Plan 4's section 1 is accepted, and on the six subsidiary questions put to this seat. It rules on no scientific quantity, no claim wording, no ledger entry, no gate state, no source file and no open release decision. I read no sealed label, ran no paid command, spent nothing, edited nothing, committed nothing, pushed nothing, and wrote exactly one file: this record. Commands run, all read-only: `git status --porcelain`, `git log --oneline`, `uv run pytest -q` (353 passed), `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy`, `uv run conformalextract verify-claims` (14/12, exit 0), and two in-process scans of the amendment text using claims.FORBIDDEN_WORDINGS and claims.CLAIM_ID (zero hits each).
acceptance_rule: The implementer builds against section 1 as written: seven items, staged privately per section 11 R2, published in section 11 R3's order. Nothing in this record needs to be discharged before that work begins. R2 applies only if the amendment document is committed; R3-R6 are for whoever next touches the accepted plan or proposes a sequencing change, and none of them blocks R1.
